candidate_nodes.label: lem:mw_i_3_compact_subgroup_bch
candidate_nodes.remark: The exact lattice exponents in 1.3(2)-(3) are OCR-damaged and should be transcribed visually before admission.
candidate_nodes.source_note: Conservative extraction of Lemma I.3 keeping the subgroup conclusion and the two valuation estimates without trusting every damaged exponent.
candidate_nodes.statement: Assume e > 2d. Then there exists B > 3d such that for every n > B the exponential map is defined and injective on varpi^n E with inverse log, and exp(varpi^n E) is a subgroup of G. For n,m > B, the logarithm of exp X exp Z and the conjugation of Z by exp X satisfy the BCH and commutator error estimates recorded in 1.3(2)-(3).

candidate_nodes.label: lem:mw_i_6_character_stabilizer
candidate_nodes.remark: The exact name of the Lie algebra lattice in 1.6(i) and the typography of Y_sharp in 1.6(iii) should be checked against the PDF.
candidate_nodes.source_note: Lemma I.6 is extracted at the level of its three numbered conclusions: existence of the Lie-algebra character, existence of chi_n on G_n, and stabilizer control.
candidate_nodes.statement: For n >= B, the functional X |-> psi(tr(varpi^(-2n) Y X)) restricts to a Lie algebra character on the lattice used to define G_n, and gamma |-> psi(tr(varpi^(-2n) Y log gamma)) defines a character chi_n of G_n. If B <= m <= n and gamma in G_m stabilizes chi_n, then gamma lies in G_n exp(varpi^m (Y_sharp intersect L)).

candidate_nodes.label: lem:mw_i_10_nonzero_invariants
candidate_nodes.remark: The opening symbol naming the Whittaker space is damaged in OCR, but the lemma statement explicitly asserts eventual nonvanishing of both W_n and W_n'.
candidate_nodes.source_note: Lemma I.10 is the finite-level nonvanishing step from nonzero degenerate Whittaker forms to the spaces W_n and W_n'.
candidate_nodes.statement: If the degenerate Whittaker space attached to the fixed nilpotent datum is nonzero, then for all sufficiently large n both auxiliary spaces W_n and W_n' are nonzero.

candidate_nodes.label: prop:mw_i_11_orbit_from_whittaker
candidate_nodes.remark: The proof uses the finite-level spaces W_n together with the Fourier transform of the test functions phi_n; the displayed formulas are noisy but the proposition statement itself is legible.
candidate_nodes.source_note: Proposition I.11 gives the direction from nonzero degenerate Whittaker forms to a nilpotent orbit with nonzero character-expansion coefficient.
candidate_nodes.statement: If the degenerate Whittaker space attached to Y is nonzero, then there exists a nilpotent orbit O in g that occurs with nonzero coefficient in the local character expansion of tr pi near the identity and whose closure contains Y.

candidate_nodes.label: lem:mw_i_12_dimension_coefficient
candidate_nodes.remark: The orbit-integral computation is OCR-damaged, but the lemma statement and the final equality dim W_n = c_O are clearly stated.
candidate_nodes.source_note: Lemma I.12 identifies the eventual dimension of W_n with the coefficient of a maximal orbit in the local character expansion.
candidate_nodes.statement: Let O = G.Y and suppose its coefficient c_O in 1.8 is nonzero and Y does not lie in the closure of any other orbit with nonzero coefficient in 1.8. Then for all sufficiently large n, dim W_n is finite, independent of n, and equal to c_O.

candidate_nodes.label: lem:mw_i_13_trivial_action
candidate_nodes.remark: The exact lattice condition on X is not safely recoverable from the OCR and should be transcribed from the PDF before admission.
candidate_nodes.source_note: Lemma I.13 is extracted at the level of its normalizing, stabilizing, and eventual triviality conclusions.
candidate_nodes.statement: Fix c > B. If X belongs to the deep lattice inside L intersect Y_sharp specified in 1.13, then exp X normalizes G_n and stabilizes chi_n. Hence exp X acts on W_n, and for n sufficiently large this action is trivial.

candidate_nodes.label: prop:mw_i_14_jacquet_injection
candidate_nodes.remark: The source labels 1.14 as a corollary; it is staged here as a proposition because the current KB schema has no corollary kind.
candidate_nodes.source_note: Corollary I.14 packages the injectivity and image description needed for the final proof of Chapter I.
candidate_nodes.statement: For n sufficiently large, in the diagram at the end of 1.9 the maps j and j' are injective, and the image of j' is the L'-fixed subspace of the Jacquet quotient appearing there.

candidate_nodes.label: lem:mw_i_15_transition_injective
candidate_nodes.remark: The composite-operator calculation following the statement is OCR-damaged, but the lemma statement itself is clean.
candidate_nodes.source_note: Lemma I.15 is the eventual injectivity statement for the transition maps between the finite-level spaces.
candidate_nodes.statement: For n sufficiently large, the transition map I_{n,n+1} is injective.

candidate_nodes.label: prop:mw_ii_1_3_regular_principal_series_orbits
candidate_nodes.remark: The proof uses several external references and induction formulas; the statement is legible but the notation around the index F should be checked to avoid confusion with the base field.
candidate_nodes.source_note: Proposition II.1.3 identifies the maximal character-expansion orbits for regular principal-series constituents of split classical groups.
candidate_nodes.statement: Let F_idx be an element of the indexing set J from II.1, with associated constituent pi_F and standard parabolic P_F. The maximal elements of N_tr(pi_F) are exactly the nilpotent orbits in g whose intersection with the Lie algebra u_F of the unipotent radical of P_F contains an open subset. These orbits are all contained in the Richardson orbit Omega_F of P_F.

candidate_nodes.label: prop:mw_ii_2_gl_n_unique_nilpotent_orbit
candidate_nodes.remark: The later segment and multisegment formulas are heavily OCR-damaged, but the proposition statement itself is clear.
candidate_nodes.source_note: Section II.2 begins with the basic uniqueness proposition for GL_n before specializing to segments and multisegments.
candidate_nodes.statement: For any smooth irreducible representation pi of GL_n(F), the maximal elements of N_tr(pi) are contained in a unique nilpotent orbit of gl_n, denoted X_tr(pi).

candidate_nodes.label: lem:mw_ii_3_2_concentration_criterion
candidate_nodes.remark: The decomposition and projection notation in the OCR should be visually checked before admission, but the logical form of the equivalence is legible.
candidate_nodes.source_note: Lemma II.3.2 relates Howe-style concentration on an orbit in S^2(X^*) to the projections of the nilpotent orbits attached to the character expansion.
candidate_nodes.statement: Let beta be an orbit in S^2(X^*), and let (pi,W) be an irreducible representation of Sp(2n,F). Then W is concentrated on beta if and only if for every orbit O in the source's character-expansion set attached to pi and every Y in O, the S^2(X^*)-projection Y_minus lies in the closure of beta, and for at least one such Y it lies in beta itself.

issues.description: Lemma I.3 has OCR damage in the BCH remainder exponents and in the conjugation estimate of 1.3(2)-(3); those exact valuations should be transcribed visually before admission.
Lemma I.6 has OCR damage in the name of the Lie algebra lattice carrying the character in 1.6(i) and in the notation of the stabilizer lattice in 1.6(iii).
The lattice condition on X in Lemma I.13 and several convolution formulas in its proof are OCR-damaged; the statement should be checked against the PDF before canonical admission.

Proposition II.1.3 depends on several external references, including Rodier, Lusztig-Spaltenstein, Springer-Steinberg, and a cited lemma [IRa]; these should be identified before proof work or admission decisions.
Section II.2 appeals repeatedly to Zelevinsky and earlier GL_n results for segments, multisegments, and induction formulas; those references should be identified before proof extraction.

The supplied II.3.1 span begins after the preceding argument and then starts the small-rank setup; it does not contain the full statement of the proposition described in the span metadata, so no candidate node was proposed for II.3.1.
Lemma II.3.2 has OCR damage in the decomposition notation Y = Y_minus + Y_0 + Y_plus and in the closure condition on the projected orbit; visual transcription is needed before canonical admission.
The supplied II.3.3 span only contains the end of the proof of II.3.2; the actual statement of the lemma described in the metadata is not present, so no candidate node was proposed for II.3.3.

notation_contexts.label: ctx:mw_chapter_i_auxiliary_spaces
notation_contexts.statement: In Chapter I, the paper works with compact open subgroups G_n carrying characters chi_n and auxiliary spaces W_n and W_n'. These spaces are compared with Jacquet-type quotients and are used to detect nonzero degenerate Whittaker forms.

notation_contexts.label: ctx:mw_regular_principal_series_indexing
notation_contexts.statement: In II.1, an element of J indexes a regular-principal-series constituent pi_F together with a standard parabolic P_F and its unipotent radical U_F; the source uses the letter F both for the base field and for this index.

notation_contexts.label: ctx:mw_small_rank_projection_notation
notation_contexts.statement: In II.3, the paper identifies S^2(X^*) with the Lie algebra of the unipotent radical opposite to P(X), decomposes g as S^2(X^*) plus Lie GL(X) plus S^2(X), and writes Y = Y_minus + Y_0 + Y_plus for the corresponding components.

payload.summary: Proposed 11 conservative body-result candidates from Chapter I and II: technical lemmas I.3 and I.6, the Chapter I chain I.10 through I.15, Proposition II.1.3 on regular principal series, Proposition II.2 on the unique GL_n orbit, and Lemma II.3.2 on concentration. I.16 and I.17 were not reproposed because their content is already represented by ext:moeglin_waldspurger_main_theorem, and II.3.1 and II.3.3 were flagged because the supplied spans do not contain their full statements.
